title: Physical Installations

header.html: 2.4 Explain important factors of physical installations: locations (IDF, MDF), rack size, port-side exhaust and intake, cabling (patch panel, fiber distribution panel), lockable racks; power (UPS, PDU, power load, voltage); environmental factors (humidity, fire suppression, temperature)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Locations

Term Meaning
MDF (main distribution frame) The central wiring room where the provider connects and core equipment sits
IDF (intermediate distribution frame) A wiring closet on a floor or area that connects end devices and links back to the MDF

2Racks and cabling

Item Detail
Rack size 19-inch wide standard rack; height in rack units (U), where 1U = 1.75 inches; common racks are 42U
Port-side exhaust / intake Airflow direction of a device: mount it so intake faces the cold aisle and exhaust faces the hot aisle, or it recirculates hot air and overheats
Patch panel Permanent cabling terminates at the panel; short patch cords link it to switches, which keeps cabling tidy and easy to change
Fiber distribution panel The patch panel for fiber
Lockable racks Physical security against tampering and unauthorized access
Exam tip

. Intake faces the cold aisle; exhaust faces the hot aisle. A switch mounted backwards (port-side exhaust in a cold aisle) overheats.

3Power

Item Meaning
UPS (uninterruptible power supply) Battery backup that keeps equipment running during short outages and cleans the power while a generator starts
PDU (power distribution unit) Distributes power to the devices in a rack; metered or switched models report load and let you power-cycle outlets remotely
Power load The total power the devices draw; do not exceed circuit or UPS capacity
Voltage Use the voltage the equipment needs (for example 120 V or 208/240 V)

4Environmental factors

Factor Goal
Temperature Keep within the manufacturer's range (cool, steady); hot aisle/cold aisle layout
Humidity Not too dry (static electricity) and not too damp (corrosion, condensation)
Fire suppression Clean-agent gas or pre-action systems in server rooms; water sprinklers can destroy equipment
Exam tip

. UPS = battery; PDU = power distribution in the rack; MDF = main room; IDF = floor closet.

Exam tip

. Intake faces the cold aisle and exhaust faces the hot aisle. A backwards switch overheats.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Equipment in a rack must keep running for a few minutes during a power outage. Which device fits?

  • AAn uninterruptible power supply
  • BA patch panel
  • CA fiber distribution panel
  • DA lockable cabinet
Show the answer

Answer: A. A UPS provides battery backup.

S2Which room is where the service provider connects and core equipment is typically located?

  • AAn intermediate distribution frame
  • BA telecommunications outlet
  • CA hot aisle
  • DThe main distribution frame
Show the answer

Answer: D. The MDF is the central wiring room.

S3A newly mounted switch overheats because its exhaust faces the cold aisle. What should be corrected?

  • AThe airflow direction, so intake faces the cold aisle
  • BThe patch panel labeling
  • CThe rack height in U
  • DThe humidity setting
Show the answer

Answer: A. Port-side exhaust and intake must match the aisle layout.

S4An administrator wants to power-cycle a hung device in a remote rack. Which device helps?

  • AA switched or managed PDU
  • BA passive patch panel
  • CA basic UPS only
  • DA fiber panel
Show the answer

Answer: A. Switched PDUs let you cycle outlets remotely.

S5Which fire suppression method is preferred in a server room?

  • AA clean-agent gas system
  • BOverhead water sprinklers alone
  • CA hand-held water hose
  • DA wet chemical kitchen system
Show the answer

Answer: A. Clean agents suppress fire without damaging electronics.

S6How tall is a 2U device?

  • A3.5 inches
  • B1.75 inches
  • C5.25 inches
  • D7 inches
Show the answer

Answer: A. One rack unit is 1.75 inches, so 2U is 3.5 inches.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is an IDF?

Show the answer

A wiring closet connecting end devices on a floor or area.

R2What does a PDU do?

Show the answer

Distributes power to the devices in a rack.

R3What is a rack unit?

Show the answer

1.75 inches of vertical rack space.

R4Which aisle should equipment intake face?

Show the answer

The cold aisle.

R5Name two environmental factors.

Show the answer

For example temperature and humidity (and fire suppression).

R6What does a patch panel do?

Show the answer

Terminates permanent cabling so short patch cords link devices.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Locations MDF (main room), IDF (floor closet)
Racks 19 inch, units of 1.75 in, intake cold aisle, exhaust hot aisle, patch and fiber panels, lockable
Power UPS (battery), PDU (distribution), load, voltage
Environment temperature, humidity, clean-agent fire suppression
